facts.statement: Richard Lydekker described the genus Suchodus in 1890 based on a fragment of a lower jaw found near Peterborough.
facts.quote: Suchodus was originally described by Richard Lydekker in 1890, based on a flattened front part of a lower jaw (NHMUK PV R 1994) collected from the Oxford Clay near Peterborough

facts.statement: Suchodus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic periods in England and France.
facts.quote: Suchodus is an extinct genus of metriorhynchid thalattosuchian from the Middle to Late Jurassic period of England and France

facts.statement: Suchodus was a fully marine reptile that fed on other large marine animals.
facts.quote: It was a fully marine reptile that would have fed on other large marine fauna.

facts.statement: Suchodus belongs to the metriorhynchid subfamily Geosaurinae and the tribe Geosaurini.
facts.quote: Suchodus is a member of the metriorhynchid subfamily called Geosaurinae and the derived tribe Geosaurini.

facts.statement: Suchodus was a large marine predator with a streamlined body, powerful tail, and long jaws lined with sharp teeth.
facts.quote: Members were generally large marine predators, adapted to open-ocean life with streamlined bodies, powerful tails, and long, robust jaws lined with sharp teeth.

facts.statement: Andrews considered Suchodus a junior synonym of Metriorhynchus in 1913.
facts.quote: The genus was regarded as a junior synonym of Metriorhynchus by Andrews, 1913.

facts.statement: Studies from the 2000s questioned whether Suchodus is a synonym of Metriorhynchus.
facts.quote: Later studies from the 2000s onwards questioned this synonymy.

facts.statement: Some authors include the species S. brachyrhynchus, originally described from the Callovian of Normandy, within the genus Suchodus.
facts.quote: Some authors have also included the species "S." brachyrhynchus, originally described for a specimen from the Callovian of Mesnil Bavent, Normandy, within the genus.

facts.statement: The placement of S. brachyrhynchus in Suchodus is debated, with some assigning it to Metriorhynchus or a new genus.
facts.quote: Its placement in Suchodus has been questioned, and it has otherwise assigned to the genus Metriorhynchus or argued that it should be placed in its own new genus.

facts.statement: Suchodus was an extinct genus of marine crocodiliforms that lived in England and France during the Middle and Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Suchodus es un género extinto de crocodiliformes marinos que vivieron durante los períodos Jurásico Medio y Jurásico Superior de Inglaterra y Francia.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses have confirmed that Suchodus, meaning "crocodile tooth" in ancient Greek, is a valid genus of metriorhynchid.
facts.quote: Análisis filogenéticos recientes han demostrado que Suchodus (nombre procedente del griego antiguo, que significa "diente de cocodrilo") es efectivamente un género válido de metriorrínquido.

facts.statement: S. brachyrhynchus lived in Western Europe (England and France) from the Middle to Late Jurassic (Callovian and Oxfordian periods).
facts.quote: S. brachyrhynchus: Europa Occidental (Inglaterra y Francia) del Jurásico Medio a Superior (periodos Calloviano y Oxfordiense)

facts.statement: S. durobrivensis was originally the type species of Suchodus but was later considered a junior synonym of Metriorhynchus by Andrews in 1913.
facts.quote: S. durobrivensis: Europa Occidental (Inglaterra y Francia) del Jurásico Medio (Calloviano). Fue originalmente la especie tipo del género Suchodus, pero fue más tarde considerada un sinónimo más moderno del género Metriorhynchus por Andrews, en 1913.

facts.statement: The time range for Suchodus is the Callovian, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)
